angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 47,050,887 km at 115.47 pc = 5.45 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 84380: distance 115.473 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.014), at which the luminosity and radius hold (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 115.473 +/- 1.617 pc; Gaia DR3 parallax 8.8991 +/- 0.1323 mas (same row, RUWE 2.79), 67.3 standard errors, is not used
radiusSource: Radius 67.631 solar radii from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 84380: radius 67.631 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 1255.76 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.061) and temperature (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 47,050,887 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 4181 +/- 125 K from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 84380: effective temperature 4181 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.116) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 84380: effective temperature 4181 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.116) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433)
spectralTypeSource: SIMBAD, * pi. Her: spectral type K3II (1989ApJS...71..245K)
objectTypeSource: SIMBAD, * pi. Her: main object type *, Star
projectedRotationSpeedSource: SIMBAD, * pi. Her: projected rotation speed 1.3 km/s, the measurement SIMBAD prefers (2005yCat.3244....0G)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's measured spectrum (HST/STIS Next Generation Spectral Library v2 (Heap & Lindler; MAST high-level science product), HD 156283) (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
